class PassOrderExecutionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def _sweep(self, sample, ast, arguments, expected, order_names):
        """Compile+run every order fresh; return {name: RunResult}.

        The pinned expectation is ground truth; the default-order run must
        meet it, and every candidate triple must equal the baseline triple
        exactly (exit status, stdout, stderr as raw values).
        """
        results = {}
        targets = {}
        for order_name in order_names:
            target = _compile_or_fail(
                sample, ast, order_name, LEGAL_ORDERS[order_name])
            result = execute_target(target, arguments)
            results[order_name] = result
            targets[order_name] = target

        expected_rc, expected_out = expected
        expected_result = RunResult(expected_rc, expected_out, b"")
        baseline = results[BASELINE_NAME]
        self.assertEqual(
            baseline.triple(), expected_result.triple(),
            msg=(f"sample {sample!r} arguments {arguments!r}: default-order "
                 f"run disagrees with the pinned source semantics\n"
                 f"{_format_triple(baseline)}"),
        )
        # Non-vacuous: the stdout channel is actually exercised, and stderr
        # stays empty on every normal run.
        self.assertTrue(
            baseline.stdout, msg=f"sample {sample!r} produced no stdout")
        self.assertEqual(baseline.stderr, b"")

        for order_name in order_names:
            if order_name == BASELINE_NAME:
                continue
            candidate = results[order_name]
            self.assertEqual(
                candidate.triple(), baseline.triple(),
                msg=_mismatch_message(
                    sample, ast, arguments, BASELINE_NAME, order_name,
                    baseline, candidate),
            )
        return targets, results

    def test_forward_sweep_all_orders_run_identically(self):
        for sample, builder, rows in _CORPUS:
            ast = builder()
            for arguments, rc, out in rows:
                with self.subTest(sample=sample, arguments=arguments,
                                  sweep="forward"):
                    self._sweep(sample, ast, arguments, (rc, out),
                                _ORDER_NAMES)

    def test_reverse_sweep_reaches_the_same_conclusion(self):
        # Visiting the orders in the reverse direction must not change any
        # verdict: each compilation/run still happens in its own fresh
        # context, so nothing from an earlier order may leak into a later
        # one regardless of scheduling direction.
        for sample, builder, rows in _CORPUS:
            ast = builder()
            for arguments, rc, out in rows:
                with self.subTest(sample=sample, arguments=arguments,
                                  sweep="reverse"):
                    self._sweep(sample, ast, arguments, (rc, out),
                                list(reversed(_ORDER_NAMES)))

    def test_reverse_sample_order_still_matches(self):
        # Isolation across samples as well: execute the whole corpus in
        # reverse, then forward, and demand identical triples from the two
        # independent runs.
        plan = []
        for sample, builder, rows in _CORPUS:
            for arguments, rc, out in rows:
                plan.append((sample, builder(), arguments, rc, out))

        def run_all(ordered):
            seen = {}
            for sample, ast, arguments, _rc, _out in ordered:
                target = _compile_or_fail(
                    sample, ast, BASELINE_NAME, DEFAULT_ORDER)
                seen[(sample, arguments)] = execute_target(target, arguments)
            return seen

        forward = run_all(plan)
        backward = run_all(list(reversed(plan)))
        self.assertEqual(
            {key: value.triple() for key, value in forward.items()},
            {key: value.triple() for key, value in backward.items()},
            msg="corpus execution order changed observable results",
        )


class TargetReproducibilityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_same_source_and_order_compiles_byte_identically(self):
        for sample, builder, _rows in _CORPUS:
            ast = builder()
            for order_name, order in LEGAL_ORDERS.items():
                with self.subTest(sample=sample, order=order_name):
                    artifacts = [
                        _compile_or_fail(sample, ast, order_name, order)
                        for _ in range(3)
                    ]
                    first, second, third = artifacts
                    if first != second:
                        self.fail(_reproducibility_message(
                            sample, order_name, first, second))
                    if second != third:
                        self.fail(_reproducibility_message(
                            sample, order_name, second, third))

    def test_reproduced_artifacts_run_identically(self):
        # Byte identity of the compiled target plus identical execution of
        # independently produced copies.
        for sample, builder, rows in _CORPUS:
            ast = builder()
            for arguments, rc, out in rows:
                for order_name, order in LEGAL_ORDERS.items():
                    with self.subTest(sample=sample, arguments=arguments,
                                      order=order_name):
                        first = _compile_or_fail(
                            sample, ast, order_name, order)
                        second = _compile_or_fail(
                            sample, ast, order_name, order)
                        self.assertEqual(first, second)
                        run_a = execute_target(first, arguments)
                        run_b = execute_target(second, arguments)
                        self.assertEqual(
                            run_a.triple(), run_b.triple(),
                            msg=(f"identical target bytes executed "
                                 f"differently: {sample!r} {order_name!r} "
                                 f"{arguments!r}\n"
                                 f"{_format_triple(run_a)}\n"
                                 f"{_format_triple(run_b)}"),
                        )
                        self.assertEqual(run_a.triple(), (rc, out, b""))

    def test_canonical_orders_share_the_fixed_point_but_raw_core_differs(
            self):
        # Guard against vacuous equivalence: the canonical alternatives
        # reach one fixed-point artifact, while the deliberately
        # un-canonicalized raw core emits different bytes.  Execution
        # equivalence (proved elsewhere) must not rest on text identity.
        for sample, builder, _rows in _CORPUS:
            ast = builder()
            with self.subTest(sample=sample):
                canonical = compile_target(ast, DEFAULT_ORDER)
                for name in _CANONICAL_ALTERNATIVES:
                    self.assertEqual(
                        canonical, compile_target(ast, LEGAL_ORDERS[name]),
                        msg=f"{sample!r}: {name!r} did not reach the "
                            "canonical fixed point",
                    )
                raw = compile_target(
                    ast, LEGAL_ORDERS[
                        "raw-core ssa,fold,licm,dce (no trailing "
                        "canonicalization)"])
                # The void sample may legitimately coincide textually once
                # numbering happens to match; require at least most corpus
                # programs to exhibit the intended textual difference.
        differing = sum(
            compile_target(builder(), DEFAULT_ORDER)
            != compile_target(
                builder(),
                LEGAL_ORDERS["raw-core ssa,fold,licm,dce (no trailing "
                             "canonicalization)"])
            for _sample, builder, _rows in _CORPUS
        )
        self.assertGreaterEqual(
            differing, len(_CORPUS) - 1,
            msg="raw-core targets should be byte-different from the "
                "canonical target for the DCE-numbering-sensitive samples",
        )


class StageContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The execution harness keeps the existing preconditions and defaults."""

    def test_every_order_starts_with_ssa_and_ends_with_rendering(self):
        for name, order in LEGAL_ORDERS.items():

                order[0], "ssa",
                msg=f"order {name!r} does not construct SSA first")
            self.assertNotIn(
                "isel", order,

            seen_ssa = False

            apply_order(lowered, ("dce", "ssa"))

        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):

    def test_unknown_pass_rejected(self):
        lowered = lower_module(_unreachable_branch_program())

    def test_default_order_is_the_documented_pipeline(self):
        # The harness's default is literally

        ast = _loop_invariant_program()

1	"""Semantic-equivalence tests for the non-SSA -> pruned SSA conversion.
2	
3	The existing tests compare node structure and rendered text.  This module
4	instead *executes* both flavors of IR and proves that, for one and the same
5	lowered program, :func:`to_ssa` preserves observable behavior:
6	
7	* the entry function is invoked with fixed, concrete arguments;
8	* the non-SSA :class:`Module` returned by ``lower_module`` and the new SSA
9	  :class:`Module` returned by ``to_ssa`` are each interpreted independently;
10	* the return value and the ordered trace of function calls
11	  ``(callee name, positional argument tuple)`` must be identical.
12	
13	The interpreter is deliberately small and works over both IR flavors:
14	
15	* non-SSA state is a mutable slot file (parameters / ``let`` variables) plus
16	  temporary storage, so the multi-written result temporary of a
17	  short-circuit operation simply holds whichever write the executed path
18	  performed;
19	* SSA state is a map of unique :class:`Temp` definitions.  Phi inputs are
20	  chosen from the block *actually arrived from*, so a loop header reads its
21	  entry values on the first visit and the current round's values on every
22	  back edge.
23	
24	Calls that did not happen (untaken ``if`` branches, unevaluated right
25	operands of short-circuit ``and``/``or``, zero-trip loops) therefore never
26	appear in the trace.
27	
28	Everything here is deterministic and standard-library-only; the only
29	supported pipeline input is the public dict/list AST (the same subset the
30	README documents, with int/bool/void and add/sub/mul arithmetic).  Any
31	interpreter failure -- a missing block target or terminator, a phi without
32	an entry for the actual predecessor, or a read of an undefined value --
33	raises ``AssertionError``; a case is never skipped.
34	"""
35	import json
36	import unittest
37	
38	from compiler_ir import (
39	    BinOp,
40	    Branch,
41	    Call,
42	    Const,
43	    Copy,
44	    Jump,
45	    Module,
46	    Return,
47	    Slot,
48	    Temp,
49	    lower_module,
50	    to_ssa,
51	)
52	
53	from test_pipeline import (
54	    arith,
55	    assign,
56	    block,
57	    bool_,
58	    call,
59	    compare,
60	    func,
61	    if_,
62	    int_,
63	    let,
64	    logical,
65	    param,
66	    program,
67	    ret,
68	    var,
69	    while_,
70	)

73	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
74	# IR interpreter (shared by the non-SSA and SSA modules)
75	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
76	
77	
78	# Every lowered program in this file is tiny and terminates quickly; this is
79	# only a belt-and-braces guard against an accidentally non-terminating case.
80	_STEP_LIMIT = 100_000
81	
82	_ARITH = {
83	    "add": lambda a, b: a + b,
84	    "sub": lambda a, b: a - b,
85	    "mul": lambda a, b: a * b,
86	}

88	_COMPARE = {
89	    "eq": lambda a, b: a == b,
90	    "ne": lambda a, b: a != b,
91	    "lt": lambda a, b: a < b,
92	    "le": lambda a, b: a <= b,
93	    "gt": lambda a, b: a > b,
94	    "ge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
95	}

98	def _assert(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
99	    """Every structural interpreter failure surfaces as AssertionError."""
100	    if not condition:
101	        raise AssertionError(message)
102	
103	
104	class _Interpreter:
105	    """Execute a lowered :class:`Module` of either SSA flavor.
106	
107	    A run returns ``(return_value, trace)`` where ``trace`` records, in
108	    occurrence order, one ``(function_name, (positional arguments))`` tuple
109	    per executed :class:`Call` instruction (including recursive and
110	    cross-function calls).  A void entry returns ``None``.
111	    """
112	
113	    def __init__(self, module: Module):
114	        _assert(isinstance(module, Module),
115	                f"interpreter expects a Module, got {type(module).__name__}")
116	        self.ssa = bool(module.ssa)
117	        self._functions = {fn_.name: fn_ for fn_ in module.functions}
118	
119	    def run(self, entry: str, arguments):
120	        fn_ = self._functions.get(entry)
121	        _assert(fn_ is not None, f"unknown entry function {entry!r}")
122	        arguments = tuple(arguments)
123	        _assert(
124	            len(arguments) == len(fn_.params),
125	            f"entry {entry!r} expects {len(fn_.params)} argument(s), "
126	            f"got {len(arguments)}",
127	        )
128	        trace: list[tuple[str, tuple]] = []
129	        value = self._invoke(fn_, arguments, trace)
130	        return value, trace
131	
132	    # -- one function activation -------------------------------------------
133	
134	    def _invoke(self, fn_, arguments, trace: list):
135	        # SSA: unique Temp definitions; non-SSA: mutable Slots plus Temps
136	        # (the short-circuit result temporary is written once per executed
137	        # path, so ordinary overwrite semantics suffice).
138	        definitions: dict[int, object] = {}
139	        slots: dict[int, object] = {}
140	        temps: dict[int, object] = {}
141	
142	        for parameter, argument in zip(fn_.params, arguments):
143	            if self.ssa:
144	                _assert(parameter.temp is not None,
145	                        f"SSA parameter {parameter.name!r} has no definition")
146	                definitions[id(parameter.temp)] = argument
147	            else:
148	                slots[parameter.slot.id] = argument
149	
150	        def write(ref, value) -> None:
151	            if self.ssa:
152	                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp) and not isinstance(ref, Slot),
153	                        f"{fn_.name}: non-Temp definition {ref!r} in SSA IR")
154	                definitions[id(ref)] = value
155	            elif isinstance(ref, Slot):
156	                slots[ref.id] = value
157	            else:
158	                temps[id(ref)] = value
159	
160	        def read(ref):
161	            if self.ssa:
162	                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp),
163	                        f"{fn_.name}: SSA read of non-Temp value {ref!r}")
164	                _assert(id(ref) in definitions,
165	                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined SSA value {ref}")
166	                return definitions[id(ref)]
167	            if isinstance(ref, Slot):
168	                _assert(ref.id in slots,
169	                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined slot {ref}")
170	                return slots[ref.id]
171	            _assert(id(ref) in temps,
172	                    f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined temporary {ref}")
173	            return temps[id(ref)]
174	
175	        def execute(instruction) -> None:
176	            if isinstance(instruction, Const):
177	                write(instruction.dest, instruction.value)
178	            elif isinstance(instruction, Copy):
179	                write(instruction.dest, read(instruction.src))
180	            elif isinstance(instruction, BinOp):
181	                left = read(instruction.left)
182	                right = read(instruction.right)
183	                write(instruction.dest,
184	                      _apply_binop(instruction, left, right, fn_.name))
185	            elif isinstance(instruction, Call):
186	                callee = self._functions.get(instruction.name)
187	                _assert(callee is not None,
188	                        f"{fn_.name}: call to unknown function "
189	                        f"{instruction.name!r}")
190	                values = tuple(read(operand) for operand in instruction.args)
191	                _assert(
192	                    len(values) == len(callee.params),
193	                    f"call to {instruction.name!r}: arity mismatch at run "
194	                    f"time ({len(values)} for {len(callee.params)})",
195	                )
196	                # Log at the moment the call happens, before the callee's
197	                # own calls, so the trace follows evaluation order.
198	                trace.append((instruction.name, values))
199	                write(instruction.dest,
200	                      self._invoke(callee, values, trace))
201	            else:
202	                _assert(False,
203	                        f"{fn_.name}: unknown instruction {instruction!r}")
204	
205	        known_blocks = {id(block) for block in fn_.blocks}
206	        block = fn_.entry
207	        previous = None
208	        steps_left = _STEP_LIMIT
209	
210	        while True:
211	            _assert(steps_left > 0,
212	                    f"{fn_.name}: step budget exhausted "
213	                    "(program does not terminate?)")
214	            steps_left -= 1
215	
216	            if self.ssa:
217	                # All incoming values are read off the *actual* predecessor
218	                # edge before any phi result is bound, matching phi
219	                # semantics when header phis reference one another.
220	                pending: list[tuple[Temp, object]] = []
221	                for phi in block.phis:
222	                    _assert(previous is not None,
223	                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi in entry block "
224	                            "has no predecessor edge")
225	                    source = phi.entries.get(previous)
226	                    _assert(source is not None,
227	                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi {phi.dest} has "
228	                            f"no incoming value from predecessor "
229	                            f"{previous.label}")
230	                    pending.append((phi.dest, read(source)))
231	                for destination, value in pending:
232	                    definitions[id(destination)] = value
233	            else:
234	                _assert(not block.phis,
235	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi node in non-SSA IR")
236	
237	            for instruction in block.instructions:
238	                execute(instruction)
239	
240	            terminator = block.terminator
241	            _assert(terminator is not None,
242	                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: missing terminator")
243	
244	            if isinstance(terminator, Return):
245	                if terminator.value is None:
246	                    return None
247	                return read(terminator.value)
248	
249	            if isinstance(terminator, Jump):
250	                _assert(id(terminator.target) in known_blocks,
251	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: jump to unknown block "
252	                        f"{terminator.target.label}")
253	                previous, block = block, terminator.target
254	                continue
255	
256	            if isinstance(terminator, Branch):
257	                condition = read(terminator.cond)

260	                        f"value {condition!r}")
261	                target = (terminator.true_target if condition
262	                          else terminator.false_target)
263	                _assert(id(target) in known_blocks,
264	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch to unknown block "
265	                        f"{target.label}")

275	    if instruction.kind == "arith":

277	        # Python's bool/int overlap cannot hide a lowering mix-up.
278	        _assert(type(left) is int and type(right) is int,
279	                f"{fn_name}: arithmetic {instruction.operator!r} on "
280	                f"non-int operands {left!r}, {right!r}")
281	        operation = _ARITH.get(instruction.operator)
282	        _assert(operation is not None,
283	                f"{fn_name}: unsupported arithmetic operator "
284	                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
285	        return operation(left, right)
286	
287	    if instruction.kind == "compare":
288	        _assert(type(left) == type(right),
289	                f"{fn_name}: comparison {instruction.operator!r} between "
290	                f"mismatched value types {left!r}, {right!r}")
291	        operation = _COMPARE.get(instruction.operator)
292	        _assert(operation is not None,
293	                f"{fn_name}: unsupported comparison operator "
294	                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
295	        return operation(left, right)
296	
297	    _assert(False, f"{fn_name}: unknown BinOp kind {instruction.kind!r}")

"""Semantic-equivalence tests for the non-SSA -> pruned SSA conversion.

The existing tests compare node structure and rendered text.  This module
instead *executes* both flavors of IR and proves that, for one and the same
lowered program, :func:`to_ssa` preserves observable behavior:

* the entry function is invoked with fixed, concrete arguments;
* the non-SSA :class:`Module` returned by ``lower_module`` and the new SSA
  :class:`Module` returned by ``to_ssa`` are each interpreted independently;
* the return value and the ordered trace of function calls
  ``(callee name, positional argument tuple)`` must be identical.

The interpreter is deliberately small and works over both IR flavors:

* non-SSA state is a mutable slot file (parameters / ``let`` variables) plus
  temporary storage, so the multi-written result temporary of a
  short-circuit operation simply holds whichever write the executed path
  performed;
* SSA state is a map of unique :class:`Temp` definitions.  Phi inputs are
  chosen from the block *actually arrived from*, so a loop header reads its
  entry values on the first visit and the current round's values on every
  back edge.

Calls that did not happen (untaken ``if`` branches, unevaluated right
operands of short-circuit ``and``/``or``, zero-trip loops) therefore never
appear in the trace.

Everything here is deterministic and standard-library-only; the only
supported pipeline input is the public dict/list AST (the same subset the
README documents, with int/bool/void and add/sub/mul arithmetic).  Any
interpreter failure -- a missing block target or terminator, a phi without
an entry for the actual predecessor, or a read of an undefined value --
raises ``AssertionError``; a case is never skipped.
"""
import json
import unittest

from compiler_ir import (
    BinOp,
    Branch,
    Call,
    Const,
    Copy,
    Jump,
    Module,
    Return,
    Slot,
    Temp,
    lower_module,
    to_ssa,
)

from test_pipeline import (
    arith,
    assign,
    block,
    bool_,
    call,
    compare,
    func,
    if_,
    int_,
    let,
    logical,
    param,
    program,
    ret,
    var,
    while_,
)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IR interpreter (shared by the non-SSA and SSA modules)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Every lowered program in this file is tiny and terminates quickly; this is
# only a belt-and-braces guard against an accidentally non-terminating case.
_STEP_LIMIT = 100_000

_ARITH = {
    "add": lambda a, b: a + b,
    "sub": lambda a, b: a - b,
    "mul": lambda a, b: a * b,
}

_COMPARE = {
    "eq": lambda a, b: a == b,
    "ne": lambda a, b: a != b,
    "lt": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "le": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    "gt": lambda a, b: a > b,
    "ge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
}


def _assert(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    """Every structural interpreter failure surfaces as AssertionError."""
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(message)


class _Interpreter:
    """Execute a lowered :class:`Module` of either SSA flavor.

    A run returns ``(return_value, trace)`` where ``trace`` records, in
    occurrence order, one ``(function_name, (positional arguments))`` tuple
    per executed :class:`Call` instruction (including recursive and
    cross-function calls).  A void entry returns ``None``.
    """

    def __init__(self, module: Module):
        _assert(isinstance(module, Module),
                f"interpreter expects a Module, got {type(module).__name__}")
        self.ssa = bool(module.ssa)
        self._functions = {fn_.name: fn_ for fn_ in module.functions}

    def run(self, entry: str, arguments):
        fn_ = self._functions.get(entry)
        _assert(fn_ is not None, f"unknown entry function {entry!r}")
        arguments = tuple(arguments)
        _assert(
            len(arguments) == len(fn_.params),
            f"entry {entry!r} expects {len(fn_.params)} argument(s), "
            f"got {len(arguments)}",
        )
        trace: list[tuple[str, tuple]] = []
        value = self._invoke(fn_, arguments, trace)
        return value, trace

    # -- one function activation -------------------------------------------

    def _invoke(self, fn_, arguments, trace: list):
        # SSA: unique Temp definitions; non-SSA: mutable Slots plus Temps
        # (the short-circuit result temporary is written once per executed
        # path, so ordinary overwrite semantics suffice).
        definitions: dict[int, object] = {}
        slots: dict[int, object] = {}
        temps: dict[int, object] = {}

        for parameter, argument in zip(fn_.params, arguments):
            if self.ssa:
                _assert(parameter.temp is not None,
                        f"SSA parameter {parameter.name!r} has no definition")
                definitions[id(parameter.temp)] = argument
            else:
                slots[parameter.slot.id] = argument

        def write(ref, value) -> None:
            if self.ssa:
                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp) and not isinstance(ref, Slot),
                        f"{fn_.name}: non-Temp definition {ref!r} in SSA IR")
                definitions[id(ref)] = value
            elif isinstance(ref, Slot):
                slots[ref.id] = value
            else:
                temps[id(ref)] = value

        def read(ref):
            if self.ssa:
                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp),
                        f"{fn_.name}: SSA read of non-Temp value {ref!r}")
                _assert(id(ref) in definitions,
                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined SSA value {ref}")
                return definitions[id(ref)]
            if isinstance(ref, Slot):
                _assert(ref.id in slots,
                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined slot {ref}")
                return slots[ref.id]
            _assert(id(ref) in temps,
                    f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined temporary {ref}")
            return temps[id(ref)]

        def execute(instruction) -> None:
            if isinstance(instruction, Const):
                write(instruction.dest, instruction.value)
            elif isinstance(instruction, Copy):
                write(instruction.dest, read(instruction.src))
            elif isinstance(instruction, BinOp):
                left = read(instruction.left)
                right = read(instruction.right)
                write(instruction.dest,
                      _apply_binop(instruction, left, right, fn_.name))
            elif isinstance(instruction, Call):
                callee = self._functions.get(instruction.name)
                _assert(callee is not None,
                        f"{fn_.name}: call to unknown function "
                        f"{instruction.name!r}")
                values = tuple(read(operand) for operand in instruction.args)
                _assert(
                    len(values) == len(callee.params),
                    f"call to {instruction.name!r}: arity mismatch at run "
                    f"time ({len(values)} for {len(callee.params)})",
                )
                # Log at the moment the call happens, before the callee's
                # own calls, so the trace follows evaluation order.
                trace.append((instruction.name, values))
                write(instruction.dest,
                      self._invoke(callee, values, trace))
            else:
                _assert(False,
                        f"{fn_.name}: unknown instruction {instruction!r}")

        known_blocks = {id(block) for block in fn_.blocks}
        block = fn_.entry
        previous = None
        steps_left = _STEP_LIMIT

        while True:
            _assert(steps_left > 0,
                    f"{fn_.name}: step budget exhausted "
                    "(program does not terminate?)")
            steps_left -= 1

            if self.ssa:
                # All incoming values are read off the *actual* predecessor
                # edge before any phi result is bound, matching phi
                # semantics when header phis reference one another.
                pending: list[tuple[Temp, object]] = []
                for phi in block.phis:
                    _assert(previous is not None,
                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi in entry block "
                            "has no predecessor edge")
                    source = phi.entries.get(previous)
                    _assert(source is not None,
                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi {phi.dest} has "
                            f"no incoming value from predecessor "
                            f"{previous.label}")
                    pending.append((phi.dest, read(source)))
                for destination, value in pending:
                    definitions[id(destination)] = value
            else:
                _assert(not block.phis,
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi node in non-SSA IR")

            for instruction in block.instructions:
                execute(instruction)

            terminator = block.terminator
            _assert(terminator is not None,
                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: missing terminator")

            if isinstance(terminator, Return):
                if terminator.value is None:
                    return None
                return read(terminator.value)

            if isinstance(terminator, Jump):
                _assert(id(terminator.target) in known_blocks,
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: jump to unknown block "
                        f"{terminator.target.label}")
                previous, block = block, terminator.target
                continue

            if isinstance(terminator, Branch):
                condition = read(terminator.cond)
                _assert(isinstance(condition, bool),
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch on non-bool "
                        f"value {condition!r}")
                target = (terminator.true_target if condition
                          else terminator.false_target)
                _assert(id(target) in known_blocks,
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch to unknown block "
                        f"{target.label}")
                previous, block = block, target
                continue

            _assert(False,
                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: unknown terminator "
                    f"{terminator!r}")


def _apply_binop(instruction: BinOp, left, right, fn_name: str):
    if instruction.kind == "arith":
        # The type checker guarantees plain ints; reject bools explicitly so
        # Python's bool/int overlap cannot hide a lowering mix-up.
        _assert(type(left) is int and type(right) is int,
                f"{fn_name}: arithmetic {instruction.operator!r} on "
                f"non-int operands {left!r}, {right!r}")
        operation = _ARITH.get(instruction.operator)
        _assert(operation is not None,
                f"{fn_name}: unsupported arithmetic operator "
                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
        return operation(left, right)

    if instruction.kind == "compare":
        _assert(type(left) == type(right),
                f"{fn_name}: comparison {instruction.operator!r} between "
                f"mismatched value types {left!r}, {right!r}")
        operation = _COMPARE.get(instruction.operator)
        _assert(operation is not None,
                f"{fn_name}: unsupported comparison operator "
                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
        return operation(left, right)

    _assert(False, f"{fn_name}: unknown BinOp kind {instruction.kind!r}")


def _interpret(module: Module, entry: str, arguments):
    return _Interpreter(module).run(entry, arguments)

def _identity_function(name: str):

def _positive_function():

# E) Cross-function forward calls: callers precede callees in the module.

def _failure_message(name, ast, entry, arguments, non_ssa_result,
                     ssa_result) -> str:
    return (
        f"semantic mismatch in case {name!r}, entry {entry!r}, "
        f"arguments {arguments!r}\n"
        f"reproducible AST:\n"
        f"{json.dumps(ast, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)}\n"
        f"non-SSA result (return value, call trace): {non_ssa_result!r}\n"
        f"SSA     result (return value, call trace): {ssa_result!r}"
    )


class SemanticEquivalenceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_non_ssa_and_ssa_modules_agree(self):
        for name, ast, entry, runs in _CASES:
            for arguments, expected_return, expected_trace in runs:
                with self.subTest(case=name, arguments=arguments):
                    module = lower_module(ast)
                    non_ssa_result = _interpret(module, entry, arguments)

                    ssa_module = to_ssa(module)
                    ssa_result = _interpret(ssa_module, entry, arguments)

                    self.assertEqual(
                        non_ssa_result, ssa_result,
                        msg=_failure_message(
                            name, ast, entry, arguments,
                            non_ssa_result, ssa_result),
                    )
                    # Ground-truth pin: agreement between the two forms is
                    # necessary but not sufficient, so anchor the observable
                    # result independently.
                    self.assertEqual(
                        ssa_result, (expected_return, expected_trace),
                        msg=(
                            f"case {name!r} arguments {arguments!r}: "
                            f"unexpected observable result {ssa_result!r}"
                        ),
                    )

    def test_bool_literal_branches_agree(self):
        # Direct literal-true branch through the interpreter's bool path.
        module = lower_module(_BOOL_LITERAL_AST)
        non_ssa_result = _interpret(module, "lit", ())
        ssa_result = _interpret(to_ssa(module), "lit", ())
        self.assertEqual(non_ssa_result, (True, []))
        self.assertEqual(ssa_result, (True, []))

    def test_results_are_deterministic_on_repeated_runs(self):
        def one_pass():
            observed = []
            for name, ast, entry, runs in _CASES:
                for arguments, _expected_return, _expected_trace in runs:
                    module = lower_module(ast)
                    non_ssa_result = _interpret(module, entry, arguments)
                    ssa_result = _interpret(
                        to_ssa(module), entry, arguments)
                    observed.append(
                        (name, arguments, non_ssa_result, ssa_result))
            return observed

        first = one_pass()
        second = one_pass()
        # Re-running the whole deterministic table must reproduce both the
        # exact results and the fixed _CASES (case, arguments) iteration
        # order.
        self.assertEqual(first, second)

    def test_trace_omits_calls_on_unexecuted_paths(self):
        # Focused assertions for the three "call must not happen" contexts:
        # missing-else fallthrough, short-circuit right operand, zero-trip
        # loop body.
        _, paths_ast, _, _ = _CASES[0]
        result = _interpret(to_ssa(lower_module(paths_ast)), "paths", (0,))
        self.assertEqual(result[1], [("is_big", (0,)), ("is_pos", (0,))])

        logical_ast = _logical_program()
        result = _interpret(
            to_ssa(lower_module(logical_ast)), "both", (0, 9))
        self.assertEqual(result, (False, [("positive", (0,))]))

        _, sumto_ast, _, _ = _CASES[1]
        result = _interpret(
            to_ssa(lower_module(sumto_ast)), "sumto", (0,))
        self.assertEqual(result, (0, [("positive", (0,))]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

1	"""Pass-ordering and idempotence semantic regression tests.
2	
3	The existing suites pin each pass in isolation (lowering, non-SSA -> SSA,
4	SSA constant folding, SSA dead-code elimination) and compare non-SSA vs SSA
5	behavior.  This module instead treats the compiler as a *pipeline* made of
6	the existing public entry points and checks that:
7	
8	1. One legal source program, fed through the existing entry point
9	   (:func:`lower_module`, which still runs AST validation, name resolution
10	   and type checking), produces the same observable behavior under the
11	   default optimization pipeline and every alternative *legal* pass order,
12	   using the unoptimized (non-SSA) result as the semantic baseline.
13	2. For fixed source, options and order, repeated compilations are
14	   byte-identical (determinism), while *different* orders are only required
15	   to agree on observable behavior -- never on instruction counts, SSA
16	   numbers or text layout.
17	3. Re-applying a canonical pass sequence to an optimized result changes
18	   neither the canonicalized IR nor the emitted target text (idempotence);
19	   each repeatable pass is also a fixed point on its own.  Sequences that
20	   stop short of the canonical endpoint are only required to reach it once
21	   the missing normalization is applied.
22	4. Orderings may only permute passes inside the existing stage contracts:
23	   SSA construction precedes every SSA-dependent optimization (folding and
24	   DCE), and instruction selection (the deterministic
25	   :func:`render_module` emission) runs after IR optimization.
26	
27	Passes and preconditions (nothing new is added to the compiler package)
28	-----------------------------------------------------------------------
29	
30	* ``ssa``  -- :func:`to_ssa`.  Legal on a lowered module and, as an
31	  idempotent canonicalization (clone + deterministic renumbering), on an
32	  already-SSA module.
33	* ``fold`` -- :func:`fold_constants`.  Its documented precondition is an
34	  SSA module: applying it before ``ssa`` raises ``ValueError``.  The pass is
35	  purely rewrite-in-place in the SSA slots (folded BinOps/phis become
36	  ``Const`` definitions) and never deletes a definition, a block or a call,
37	  and never turns a constant ``Branch`` into a ``Jump``.
38	* ``dce``  -- :func:`eliminate_dead_code`.  Its documented precondition is
39	  an SSA module: applying it before ``ssa`` raises ``ValueError``.
40	* instruction selection is the final :func:`render_module` and is fixed
41	  last.
42	
43	The default optimization pipeline is ``ssa, fold, dce, ssa``: both
44	SSA-dependent optimizations sit after SSA construction, folding runs before
45	DCE so that definitions made pointless by folding (folded BinOps, folded
46	phis and their operands) are reclaimed in the same pipeline, and a trailing
47	SSA canonicalization compacts the numbering holes DCE may leave so the
48	emitted IR is the canonical fixed point of the sequence.  Alternative legal
49	orders permute the middle: folding may be repeated, DCE may be repeated,
50	DCE may run before folding (a following DCE is then needed to reclaim the
51	definitions folding exposes), and fold/DCE may interleave.  Orders without
52	DCE (``ssa`` and ``ssa, fold``) and the un-canonicalized raw cores
53	(``ssa, fold, dce`` and ``ssa, dce, fold``) are legal as well; their text
54	may differ while their observable behavior must not.
55	
56	Observables
57	-----------
58	
59	The language has no I/O statement, so the ordered trace of executed calls
60	``(callee, positional args)`` is the standard-output surrogate -- the only
61	side effect the language can have (it is also the observable used by
62	``test_semantic_equivalence.py``).  An outcome is one of:
63	
64	* normal termination: return value (``None`` for ``void``) + call trace;
65	* a runtime fault: error category, trigger site, the operands at the fault,
66	  and the call trace produced *before* the fault.
67	
68	The language's grammar already includes ``div``/``mod``; the single runtime
69	error the language defines is a zero divisor.  Division and modulo follow
70	truncation toward zero (the remainder satisfies ``a == (a/b)*b + a%b``).
71	There is no array or indexing construct, so no bounds error exists in this
72	language subset, and no undefined-behavior sample is used: every faulting
73	instruction's result is consumed (returned, branched on or accumulated), so
74	no legal order can legally delete it.  The fault samples additionally cover
75	a divisor that *folds to zero* (``3 - 3``): folding must propagate the zero
76	into the faulting operand while keeping the faulting ``div``/``mod``
77	BinOp -- the trap must neither be swallowed nor advanced past the call that
78	precedes it.

81	``(function name, block label, operator, ordinal of the BinOp among the
82	BinOps of its block)``: block labels are assigned by the lowering DFS and

84	surviving BinOps is preserved as well.  Every faulting block in this suite
85	contains a single faulting BinOp, so the site is unambiguous.

88	or environment-dependent behavior, hence there is no seed to pin.

166	ZERO_DIVISOR = "division-by-zero"
167	
168	
169	def _trunc_div(a: int, b: int):
170	    """Integer division truncated toward zero; raises ZeroDivisionError."""
171	    if b == 0:
172	        raise ZeroDivisionError
173	    quotient = abs(a) // abs(b)
174	    if (a < 0) != (b < 0):
175	        quotient = -quotient
176	    return quotient
177	
178	
179	def _trunc_mod(a: int, b: int):
180	    """Truncated-toward-zero remainder; raises ZeroDivisionError."""
181	    if b == 0:
182	        raise ZeroDivisionError
183	    return a - _trunc_div(a, b) * b

187	    "add": lambda a, b: a + b,
188	    "sub": lambda a, b: a - b,
189	    "mul": lambda a, b: a * b,
190	    "div": _trunc_div,
191	    "mod": _trunc_mod,

195	    "eq": lambda a, b: a == b,
196	    "ne": lambda a, b: a != b,
197	    "lt": lambda a, b: a < b,
198	    "le": lambda a, b: a <= b,

209	class _Interpreter:
210	    """Execute a lowered :class:`Module` of either SSA flavor.
211	
212	    Mirrors the interpreter in ``test_semantic_equivalence.py`` but adds
213	    ``div``/``mod`` and converts their zero-divisor trap into a
214	    :class:`RuntimeFault` with a numbering-independent site.
215	    """
216	
217	    def __init__(self, module: Module):
218	        _assert(isinstance(module, Module),
219	                f"interpreter expects a Module, got {type(module).__name__}")
220	        self.ssa = bool(module.ssa)
221	        self._functions = {fn_.name: fn_ for fn_ in module.functions}
222	
223	    def run(self, entry: str, arguments):
224	        fn_ = self._functions.get(entry)
225	        _assert(fn_ is not None, f"unknown entry function {entry!r}")
226	        arguments = tuple(arguments)
227	        _assert(
228	            len(arguments) == len(fn_.params),
229	            f"entry {entry!r} expects {len(fn_.params)} argument(s), "
230	            f"got {len(arguments)}",
231	        )
232	        trace: list = []
233	        value = self._invoke(fn_, arguments, trace)
234	        return value, trace
235	
236	    def _invoke(self, fn_, arguments, trace: list):
237	        definitions: dict = {}
238	        slots: dict = {}
239	        temps: dict = {}
240	
241	        for parameter, argument in zip(fn_.params, arguments):
242	            if self.ssa:
243	                _assert(parameter.temp is not None,
244	                        f"SSA parameter {parameter.name!r} has no definition")
245	                definitions[id(parameter.temp)] = argument
246	            else:
247	                slots[parameter.slot.id] = argument
248	
249	        def write_ref(ref, value) -> None:
250	            if self.ssa:
251	                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp) and not isinstance(
252	                    ref, Slot),
253	                    f"{fn_.name}: non-Temp definition {ref!r} in SSA IR")
254	                definitions[id(ref)] = value
255	            elif isinstance(ref, Slot):
256	                slots[ref.id] = value
257	            else:
258	                temps[id(ref)] = value
259	
260	        def read(ref):
261	            if isinstance(ref, Slot):
262	                _assert(ref.id in slots,
263	                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined slot {ref}")
264	                return slots[ref.id]
265	            if self.ssa:
266	                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp),
267	                        f"{fn_.name}: SSA read of non-Temp value {ref!r}")
268	                _assert(id(ref) in definitions,
269	                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined SSA value {ref}")
270	                return definitions[id(ref)]
271	            _assert(id(ref) in temps,
272	                    f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined temporary {ref}")
273	            return temps[id(ref)]
274	
275	        def execute(instruction, block, binop_index) -> None:
276	            if isinstance(instruction, Const):
277	                write_ref(instruction.dest, instruction.value)
278	            elif isinstance(instruction, Copy):
279	                write_ref(instruction.dest, read(instruction.src))
280	            elif isinstance(instruction, BinOp):
281	                left = read(instruction.left)
282	                right = read(instruction.right)
283	                try:
284	                    value = _apply_binop(instruction, left, right, fn_.name)
285	                except ZeroDivisionError:
286	                    raise RuntimeFault(
287	                        ZERO_DIVISOR, fn_.name, block.label,
288	                        instruction.operator, binop_index[id(instruction)],
289	                        left, right, trace,
290	                    )
291	                write_ref(instruction.dest, value)
292	            elif isinstance(instruction, Call):
293	                callee = self._functions.get(instruction.name)
294	                _assert(callee is not None,
295	                        f"{fn_.name}: call to unknown function "
296	                        f"{instruction.name!r}")
297	                values = tuple(read(operand) for operand in instruction.args)
298	                _assert(
299	                    len(values) == len(callee.params),
300	                    f"call to {instruction.name!r}: run-time arity mismatch",
301	                )
302	                trace.append((instruction.name, values))
303	                write_ref(instruction.dest,
304	                          self._invoke(callee, values, trace))
305	            else:
306	                _assert(False,
307	                        f"{fn_.name}: unknown instruction {instruction!r}")
308	
309	        known_blocks = {id(block) for block in fn_.blocks}
310	        block = fn_.entry
311	        previous = None
312	        steps_left = _STEP_LIMIT
313	
314	        while True:
315	            _assert(steps_left > 0,
316	                    f"{fn_.name}: step budget exhausted "
317	                    "(program does not terminate?)")
318	            steps_left -= 1
319	
320	            if self.ssa:
321	                pending = []
322	                for phi in block.phis:
323	                    _assert(previous is not None,
324	                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi in entry block "
325	                            "has no predecessor edge")
326	                    source = phi.entries.get(previous)
327	                    _assert(source is not None,
328	                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi {phi.dest} has "
329	                            f"no incoming value from {previous.label}")
330	                    pending.append((phi.dest, read(source)))
331	                for destination, value in pending:
332	                    definitions[id(destination)] = value
333	            else:
334	                _assert(not block.phis,
335	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi node in non-SSA IR")
336	
337	            # Numbering-independent ordinal of each BinOp among the block's
338	            # BinOps (folding/DCE preserve their relative order).  BinOp
339	            # nodes are mutable dataclasses and therefore unhashable, so
340	            # key by id.
341	            binop_index = {
342	                id(ins): ordinal
343	                for ordinal, ins in enumerate(
344	                    ins for ins in block.instructions
345	                    if isinstance(ins, BinOp)
346	                )
347	            }
348	            for instruction in block.instructions:
349	                execute(instruction, block, binop_index)
350	
351	            terminator = block.terminator
352	            _assert(terminator is not None,
353	                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: missing terminator")
354	
355	            if isinstance(terminator, Return):
356	                return None if terminator.value is None else read(
357	                    terminator.value)
358	
359	            if isinstance(terminator, Jump):
360	                _assert(id(terminator.target) in known_blocks,
361	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: jump to unknown block "
362	                        f"{terminator.target.label}")
363	                previous, block = block, terminator.target
364	                continue
365	
366	            if isinstance(terminator, Branch):
367	                condition = read(terminator.cond)
368	                _assert(isinstance(condition, bool),
369	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch on non-bool "
370	                        f"value {condition!r}")
371	                target = (terminator.true_target if condition
372	                          else terminator.false_target)
373	                _assert(id(target) in known_blocks,
374	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch to unknown block "
375	                        f"{target.label}")
376	                previous, block = block, target
377	                continue
378	
379	            _assert(False,
380	                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: unknown terminator")
381	
382	
383	def _apply_binop(instruction: BinOp, left, right, fn_name: str):
384	    if instruction.kind == "arith":
385	        _assert(type(left) is int and type(right) is int,
386	                f"{fn_name}: arithmetic {instruction.operator!r} on "
387	                f"non-int operands {left!r}, {right!r}")
388	        operation = _ARITH.get(instruction.operator)
389	        _assert(operation is not None,
390	                f"{fn_name}: unsupported arithmetic operator "
391	                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
392	        return operation(left, right)
393	
394	    if instruction.kind == "compare":
395	        _assert(type(left) == type(right),
396	                f"{fn_name}: comparison {instruction.operator!r} between "
397	                f"mismatched value types {left!r}, {right!r}")
398	        operation = _COMPARE.get(instruction.operator)
399	        _assert(operation is not None,
400	                f"{fn_name}: unsupported comparison operator "
401	                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
402	        return operation(left, right)
403	
404	    _assert(False, f"{fn_name}: unknown BinOp kind {instruction.kind!r}")

407	class Outcome:
408	    """Observable result of one run: either a normal value or a fault."""
409	
410	    def __init__(self, kind, value=None, output=(), category=None,
411	                 site=None, operands=None):
412	        self.kind = kind  # "normal" | "fault"
413	        self.value = value
414	        self.output = list(output)
415	        self.category = category
416	        self.site = site
417	        self.operands = operands
418	
419	    @classmethod
420	    def normal(cls, value, output):
421	        return cls("normal", value=value, output=output)
422	
423	    @classmethod
424	    def fault(cls, error: RuntimeFault):
425	        return cls(
426	            "fault", output=error.output, category=error.category,
427	            site=error.site, operands=(error.left, error.right),
428	        )
429	
430	    def __eq__(self, other):
431	        if not isinstance(other, Outcome):
432	            return NotImplemented
433	        return (
434	            self.kind, self.value, self.output,
435	            self.category, self.site, self.operands,
436	        ) == (
437	            other.kind, other.value, other.output,
438	            other.category, other.site, other.operands,
439	        )
440	
441	    def __repr__(self):
442	        if self.kind == "normal":
443	            return f"Outcome.normal(value={self.value!r}, output={self.output!r})"
444	        return (
445	            f"Outcome.fault(category={self.category!r}, site={self.site!r}, "
446	            f"operands={self.operands!r}, output={self.output!r})"
447	        )
448

450	def _interpret(module: Module, entry: str, arguments) -> Outcome:
451	    try:
452	        value, trace = _Interpreter(module).run(entry, arguments)
453	    except RuntimeFault as fault:
454	        return Outcome.fault(fault)
455	    return Outcome.normal(value, trace)

459	# Pass schedules (existing passes only; stage contracts enforced)

462	
463	# SSA construction, constant folding, loop-invariant code motion, DCE,
464	# then a final SSA canonicalization (clone + deterministic renumbering),
465	# which makes the emitted IR the fixed point of the whole sequence: DCE
466	# may leave numbering holes, and the trailing ssa pass compacts them
467	# without changing structure or semantics.  Folding precedes LICM so
468	# folded loop constants are exposed, and both precede DCE on purpose so
469	# their newly dead definitions are reclaimed in the same pipeline.
470	DEFAULT_ORDER = ("ssa", "fold", "licm", "dce", "ssa")
471	
472	# Legal alternatives: an explicit fold fixpoint repeat, an explicit LICM
473	# fixpoint repeat, an explicit DCE fixpoint repeat, DCE-before-fold (a
474	# second DCE reclaims what folding exposes), and a fold/dce interleaving
475	# -- all end in the canonicalizing ssa pass, so each is a fixed point of
476	# its own sequence.
477	ALT_FOLD_FIXPOINT = ("ssa", "fold", "fold", "licm", "dce", "ssa")
478	ALT_LICM_FIXPOINT = ("ssa", "fold", "licm", "licm", "dce", "ssa")
479	ALT_DCE_FIXPOINT = ("ssa", "fold", "licm", "dce", "dce", "ssa")
480	ALT_DCE_BEFORE_FOLD = ("ssa", "dce", "fold", "licm", "dce", "ssa")
481	ALT_INTERLEAVE = ("ssa", "fold", "dce", "licm", "fold", "dce", "ssa")
482	# Legal but less optimizing: construction (+ canonicalization) only, or
483	# folding without any DCE: folded text coexists with the now-unused
484	# definitions, which is a different text shape with identical behavior.
485	NO_DCE_ORDER = ("ssa",)
486	FOLD_NO_DCE_ORDER = ("ssa", "fold")
487	# README-style raw cores without the trailing canonicalization: legal,
488	# used for cross-order semantics and determinism (their endpoints may
489	# carry numbering holes and are compared on observables, not text).
490	RAW_FOLD_DCE_ORDER = ("ssa", "fold", "licm", "dce")
491	RAW_DCE_FOLD_ORDER = ("ssa", "dce", "fold", "licm", "dce")
492	
493	LEGAL_ORDERS = {
494	    "default ssa,fold,licm,dce,ssa": DEFAULT_ORDER,
495	    "alt ssa,fold,fold,licm,dce,ssa": ALT_FOLD_FIXPOINT,
496	    "alt ssa,fold,licm,licm,dce,ssa": ALT_LICM_FIXPOINT,
497	    "alt ssa,fold,licm,dce,dce,ssa": ALT_DCE_FIXPOINT,
498	    "alt ssa,dce,fold,licm,dce,ssa": ALT_DCE_BEFORE_FOLD,
499	    "alt ssa,fold,dce,licm,fold,dce,ssa": ALT_INTERLEAVE,
500	    "no-dce ssa": NO_DCE_ORDER,
501	    "fold-no-dce ssa,fold": FOLD_NO_DCE_ORDER,
502	    "raw core ssa,fold,licm,dce": RAW_FOLD_DCE_ORDER,
503	    "raw core ssa,dce,fold,licm,dce": RAW_DCE_FOLD_ORDER,
504	}

506	# Orders whose endpoint is the canonical fixed point used by the strict
507	# idempotence test (all optimizers present, trailing renumbering).
508	CANONICAL_ORDERS = {
509	    name: order for name, order in LEGAL_ORDERS.items()
510	    if name.startswith(("default", "alt"))
511	}

513	_SSA_DEPENDENT = {"fold", "licm", "dce"}
514	_PASS_FUNCS = {
515	    "ssa": to_ssa,
516	    "fold": fold_constants,
517	    "licm": hoist_loop_invariants,
518	    "dce": eliminate_dead_code,

522	def apply_order(module: Module, order) -> Module:
523	    """Apply ``order`` (a tuple of pass names) to ``module``.
524	
525	    :raises ValueError: if a pass name is unknown, if instruction selection
526	        appears anywhere but the end, or if ``fold``/``dce`` is scheduled
527	        before the first ``ssa`` (both require an SSA module).
528	    """
529	    ssa_seen = bool(getattr(module, "ssa", False))
530	    for name in order:
531	        if name == "ssa":
532	            module = to_ssa(module)
533	            ssa_seen = True
534	        elif name in _SSA_DEPENDENT:
535	            if not ssa_seen:
536	                raise ValueError(
537	                    "pass order violates precondition: "
538	                    f"{name!r} requires an SSA module, but no 'ssa' pass "
539	                    "precedes it"
540	                )
541	            module = _PASS_FUNCS[name](module)
542	        elif name == "isel":
543	            raise ValueError(
544	                "pass order violates stage contract: instruction selection "
545	                "('isel') must be the final stage"
546	            )
547	        else:
548	            raise ValueError(f"unknown pass in order: {name!r}")
549	    return module

552	def compile_ast(ast: dict, order):
553	    """Compile a fresh copy of ``ast`` through lowering and ``order``.
554	
555	    Returns ``(unoptimized_module, optimized_module, target_text)`` where
556	    the target text is instruction selection (rendering) run last.
557	    """
558	    lowered = lower_module(copy.deepcopy(ast))
559	    optimized = apply_order(lowered, order)
560	    return lowered, optimized, render_module(optimized)

563	def structural_signature(module: Module):
564	    """Numbering-independent structural fingerprint of a module."""
565	    signature = []
566	    for fn_ in module.functions:
567	        blocks = []
568	        for block in fn_.blocks:
569	            instructions = []
570	            for ins in block.instructions:
571	                if isinstance(ins, Const):
572	                    instructions.append(("const", ins.value))
573	                elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
574	                    instructions.append(("copy",))
575	                elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
576	                    instructions.append((ins.kind, ins.operator))
577	                elif isinstance(ins, Call):
578	                    instructions.append(("call", ins.name, len(ins.args)))
579	            terminator = type(block.terminator).__name__
580	            blocks.append((
581	                block.id, terminator, len(block.phis),
582	                tuple(instructions),
583	            ))
584	        signature.append((
585	            fn_.name, fn_.ret_type,
586	            tuple((p.name, p.temp.type if p.temp is not None
587	                   else p.slot.type) for p in fn_.params),
588	            tuple(blocks),
589	        ))
590	    return tuple(signature)
591

593	def definition_count(module: Module) -> int:
594	    """Count parameter, phi and instruction definitions per function."""
595	    total = 0
596	    for fn_ in module.functions:
597	        total += len(fn_.params)
598	        for block in fn_.blocks:
599	            total += len(block.phis) + len(block.instructions)
600	    return total

608	def _emit_function(name="emit"):
609	    return func(name, [param("v", "int")], "int", [ret(var("v"))])
610	
611	
612	# A) Constants and phi propagation at a branch convergence.
613	#
614	# `a` is the same dominating constant on BOTH outgoing edges, so its merge
615	# phi is trivial (one incoming SSA value) and is pruned during SSA
616	# construction; the returned value is that constant propagated through the
617	# join.  `b` carries genuinely different values per edge and needs a real
618	# merge phi consumed by a side-effecting call.
619	def _join_program():
620	    return program(
621	        func("join", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
622	            let("k", "int", int_(7)),
623	            let("a", "int", int_(0)),
624	            if_(var("c"), [assign("a", var("k"))],
625	                 [assign("a", var("k"))]),
626	            let("b", "int", int_(0)),
627	            if_(var("c"),
628	                [assign("b", arith("add", var("x"), int_(1)))],
629	                [assign("b", arith("sub", var("x"), int_(1)))]),
630	            let("s", "int", call("emit", [var("b")])),
631	            ret(arith("add", var("a"), var("s"))),
632	        ]),
633	        _emit_function(),
634	    )
635	
636	
637	# B) Deletable pure computations vs. still-side-effecting expressions.
638	#
639	# `d` and `junk` are pure chains nobody consumes: DCE deletes them (and
640	# their constants), but BOTH calls remain roots even though `ignored`'s
641	# result is never read -- deleting either would drop observable output.
642	def _clean_program():
643	    return program(
644	        func("clean", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
645	            let("d", "int",
646	                arith("mul", arith("add", int_(1), int_(2)), int_(3))),
647	            let("keptarg", "int", arith("add", var("n"), int_(10))),
648	            let("v", "int", call("observe", [var("keptarg")])),
649	            let("ignored", "int", call("observe", [int_(99)])),
650	            let("junk", "int",
651	                arith("add", arith("mul", var("v"), int_(3)), var("d"))),
652	            ret(arith("add", var("v"), int_(4))),
653	        ]),
654	        _emit_function("observe"),
655	    )
656	
657	
658	# C) Loop-invariant value plus a conditional branch inside the loop.
659	#
660	# `base` is loop invariant and defined before the header; the loop still
661	# carries real header phis for `i` and `total`, and the in-loop if makes the
662	# side-effecting call happen only on iterations that take its else edge.
663	def _loop_program():
664	    return program(
665	        func("loopsum", [param("n", "int"), param("k", "int")], "int", [
666	            let("base", "int", arith("add", var("k"), int_(1))),
667	            let("total", "int", int_(0)),
668	            let("i", "int", int_(0)),
669	            while_(compare("lt", var("i"), var("n")), [
670	                if_(compare("gt", var("i"), int_(1)),
671	                    [assign("total", arith(
672	                        "add",
673	                        arith("add", var("total"), var("base")),
674	                        var("i")))],
675	                    [
676	                        let("t", "int", call("ping", [var("i")])),
677	                        assign("total", arith("add", var("total"), var("t"))),
678	                    ]),
679	                assign("i", arith("add", var("i"), int_(1))),
680	            ]),
681	            ret(var("total")),
682	        ]),
683	        _emit_function("ping"),
684	    )
685	
686	
687	# D) An inlineable call with dead code introduced after it.
688	#
689	# `dbl` is a trivial inline candidate; no pass order actually inlines it, so
690	# every order keeps the call and its observable position.  The pure
691	# computations built AFTER the call (`junk1`, `junk2`) are dead and vanish
692	# under DCE, while the later side-effecting call `after` is preserved.
693	def _around_program():
694	    return program(
695	        func("around", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
696	            let("v", "int", call("dbl", [arith("add", var("n"), int_(1))])),
697	            let("junk1", "int", arith("mul", var("v"), int_(9))),
698	            let("junk2", "int", arith("add", var("junk1"), int_(5))),
699	            let("w", "int", call("after", [var("v")])),
700	            ret(var("v")),
701	        ]),
702	        func("dbl", [param("x", "int")], "int",
703	             [ret(arith("mul", var("x"), int_(2)))]),
704	        _emit_function("after"),
705	    )
706	
707	
708	# F) Cross-basic-block constant propagation with no phi.
709	#
710	# `k = 1 + 2` is defined once in the entry block and read on BOTH sides of
711	# the branch: in the then arm as the side-effecting call's argument, and
712	# after the join through `k * 4`.  Folding propagates the literal 3 (and
713	# the folded 12) across block boundaries without inserting a phi or moving
714	# the call; the arm call simply does not happen on the false path.
715	def _cross_block_program():
716	    return program(
717	        func("cross", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
718	            let("k", "int", arith("add", int_(1), int_(2))),
719	            if_(var("c"), [let("h", "int", call("mark", [var("k")]))], []),
720	            let("r", "int", arith("mul", var("k"), int_(4))),
721	            let("e", "int", call("emit", [var("r")])),
722	            ret(arith("add", var("e"), var("x"))),
723	        ]),
724	        _emit_function("mark"),
725	        _emit_function(),
726	    )
727	
728	
729	# G) Same-literal merge phi folded via foldable arm arithmetic.
730	#
731	# Both arms compute the literal 7 (3+4 and 10-3) in their own blocks; the
732	# merge phi folds to Const 7 and the returned `a * 2` folds to 14.  The
733	# arm definitions are live BEFORE folding (they feed the phi) but dead
734	# AFTER it: only the fold-then-DCE pipeline removes them, while DCE alone
735	# keeps them.  This is the "dead definitions exposed only after folding"
736	# interaction.

743	                [assign("a", arith("sub", int_(10), int_(3)))]),

745	        ]),

1057	def _first_difference(expected: Outcome, actual: Outcome):
1058	    """Name the first observable that differs, in comparison order."""
1059	    if expected.kind != actual.kind:
1060	        return "termination kind", expected.kind, actual.kind
1061	    if expected.output != actual.output:
1062	        return "standard output (ordered call trace)", expected.output, \
1063	            actual.output
1064	    if expected.kind == "fault":
1065	        if expected.category != actual.category:
1066	            return "runtime error category", expected.category, \
1067	                actual.category
1068	        if expected.site != actual.site:
1069	            return "runtime error trigger site", expected.site, actual.site
1070	        if expected.operands != actual.operands:
1071	            return "runtime error operands", expected.operands, \
1072	                actual.operands
1073	    else:
1074	        if expected.value != actual.value:
1075	            return "return value", expected.value, actual.value
1076	    return None
1077	
1078	
1079	def _mismatch_message(label, order_name, entry, arguments, expected, actual):
1080	    diff = _first_difference(expected, actual)
1081	    header = (
1082	        f"semantic mismatch for sample {label!r}, order {order_name!r}, "
1083	        f"entry {entry!r}, arguments {arguments!r}"
1084	    )
1085	    if diff is None:
1086	        return header
1087	    field, wanted, got = diff
1088	    return (
1089	        f"{header}\n"
1090	        f"first differing observable: {field}\n"
1091	        f"  expected: {wanted!r}\n"
1092	        f"  actual:   {got!r}\n"
1093	        f"baseline outcome: {expected!r}\n"
1094	        f"this order:       {actual!r}"
1095	    )

"""Pass-ordering and idempotence semantic regression tests.

The existing suites pin each pass in isolation (lowering, non-SSA -> SSA,
SSA constant folding, SSA dead-code elimination) and compare non-SSA vs SSA
behavior.  This module instead treats the compiler as a *pipeline* made of
the existing public entry points and checks that:

1. One legal source program, fed through the existing entry point
   (:func:`lower_module`, which still runs AST validation, name resolution
   and type checking), produces the same observable behavior under the
   default optimization pipeline and every alternative *legal* pass order,
   using the unoptimized (non-SSA) result as the semantic baseline.
2. For fixed source, options and order, repeated compilations are
   byte-identical (determinism), while *different* orders are only required
   to agree on observable behavior -- never on instruction counts, SSA
   numbers or text layout.
3. Re-applying a canonical pass sequence to an optimized result changes
   neither the canonicalized IR nor the emitted target text (idempotence);
   each repeatable pass is also a fixed point on its own.  Sequences that
   stop short of the canonical endpoint are only required to reach it once
   the missing normalization is applied.
4. Orderings may only permute passes inside the existing stage contracts:
   SSA construction precedes every SSA-dependent optimization (folding and
   DCE), and instruction selection (the deterministic
   :func:`render_module` emission) runs after IR optimization.

Passes and preconditions (nothing new is added to the compiler package)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

* ``ssa``  -- :func:`to_ssa`.  Legal on a lowered module and, as an
  idempotent canonicalization (clone + deterministic renumbering), on an
  already-SSA module.
* ``fold`` -- :func:`fold_constants`.  Its documented precondition is an
  SSA module: applying it before ``ssa`` raises ``ValueError``.  The pass is
  purely rewrite-in-place in the SSA slots (folded BinOps/phis become
  ``Const`` definitions) and never deletes a definition, a block or a call,
  and never turns a constant ``Branch`` into a ``Jump``.
* ``dce``  -- :func:`eliminate_dead_code`.  Its documented precondition is
  an SSA module: applying it before ``ssa`` raises ``ValueError``.
* instruction selection is the final :func:`render_module` and is fixed
  last.

The default optimization pipeline is ``ssa, fold, dce, ssa``: both
SSA-dependent optimizations sit after SSA construction, folding runs before
DCE so that definitions made pointless by folding (folded BinOps, folded
phis and their operands) are reclaimed in the same pipeline, and a trailing
SSA canonicalization compacts the numbering holes DCE may leave so the
emitted IR is the canonical fixed point of the sequence.  Alternative legal
orders permute the middle: folding may be repeated, DCE may be repeated,
DCE may run before folding (a following DCE is then needed to reclaim the
definitions folding exposes), and fold/DCE may interleave.  Orders without
DCE (``ssa`` and ``ssa, fold``) and the un-canonicalized raw cores
(``ssa, fold, dce`` and ``ssa, dce, fold``) are legal as well; their text
may differ while their observable behavior must not.

Observables
-----------

The language has no I/O statement, so the ordered trace of executed calls
``(callee, positional args)`` is the standard-output surrogate -- the only
side effect the language can have (it is also the observable used by
``test_semantic_equivalence.py``).  An outcome is one of:

* normal termination: return value (``None`` for ``void``) + call trace;
* a runtime fault: error category, trigger site, the operands at the fault,
  and the call trace produced *before* the fault.

The language's grammar already includes ``div``/``mod``; the single runtime
error the language defines is a zero divisor.  Division and modulo follow
truncation toward zero (the remainder satisfies ``a == (a/b)*b + a%b``).
There is no array or indexing construct, so no bounds error exists in this
language subset, and no undefined-behavior sample is used: every faulting
instruction's result is consumed (returned, branched on or accumulated), so
no legal order can legally delete it.  The fault samples additionally cover
a divisor that *folds to zero* (``3 - 3``): folding must propagate the zero
into the faulting operand while keeping the faulting ``div``/``mod``
BinOp -- the trap must neither be swallowed nor advanced past the call that
precedes it.

A fault site is identified independently of SSA numbering by
``(function name, block label, operator, ordinal of the BinOp among the
BinOps of its block)``: block labels are assigned by the lowering DFS and
preserved by ``to_ssa``, folding and DCE, and the relative order of
surviving BinOps is preserved as well.  Every faulting block in this suite
contains a single faulting BinOp, so the site is unambiguous.

All inputs are fixed literal argument tuples; the pipeline has no random
or environment-dependent behavior, hence there is no seed to pin.
"""
